title: Patient Financial Assistance Program: Deduction Window for Laboratory Payments After a Loss of Coverage or With No Coverage on File
content:
**Rule.** For the laboratory-payments deduction on a Patient Financial Assistance Program case, the deduction window's length depends on the household's coverage as held in Insurance Coverage & Claims: a household with a coverage that ended fewer than 12 months before today counts the whole months from the day that coverage ended to today, plus one; a household with no coverage of any kind on file counts 18 months; for any other household this rule does not change the window's length. The window holds entries dated fewer than that number of months before today, counted in whole calendar months from the entry's date to today.

**Terms.** A coverage that ended is a coverage in terminated status, and the day it ended is its termination date; "fewer than 12 months" is counted in whole calendar months from that date to today. "No coverage of any kind on file" means no coverage record at all, whatever its status; a household with only a terminated, inactive or pending coverage has coverage on file.

## Dated cases (hypothetical; today 15 September 2026)

| Coverage on file | Whole months since it ended | Deduction window |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage terminated 2 July 2026 | 2 | 3 months: entries dated 16 June 2026 or later |
| Coverage terminated 20 September 2025 | 11 | 12 months |
| Coverage terminated 15 September 2025 | 12 | Not changed by this rule: the coverage did not end fewer than 12 months ago |
| No coverage record of any kind | Not applicable | 18 months: entries dated 16 March 2025 or later |
| An active coverage, none terminated | Not applicable | Not changed by this rule |
